paragraphs: In Tamid 29a, Rabbi Yannai bar Nachmani said this in the name of Shmuel. In Chullin 90b, Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani transmits the same teaching. Hyman considers the latter reading correct.

notes.text: Hyman’s compressed “Shmuel said” is listed under Yannai bar Nachmani; he prefers the parallel attribution to Yitzchak bar Nachmani in Chullin.

The saved whole Davidson Tamid29a scalar explicitly has Rabbi Yannai bar Nachmani reporting Shmuel; Chullin90b explicitly has Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani reporting Shmuel in the parallel exaggeration teaching. These support the two expanded titles and compressed reporting direction. Hyman endorses Yitzchak as correct; this is his preference, not a proved original text or authority merger.

The consulted texts of Tamid 29a and Chullin 90b both attribute the teaching about three instances of exaggeration to Shmuel. They differ on the transmitter, naming Yannai in Tamid and Yitzchak in Chullin. Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 765) expressly favors Yitzchak.
